titulo: The risk of optimizing against your own meter
lead: A loop that improves itself will find the shortest path to a higher score, and the shortest path isn't always improving the system: it can be memorizing the cases or tampering with the meter. In this lesson you watch both shortcuts become a keep, close them with a meter frozen outside the repo and hidden cases, and watch a real Claude change get discarded.
objetivo: catch the agent that improves the score without improving the system: a meter with a hash, kept outside the repo, and hidden cases the agent can't see.

aprende.t: Goodhart's law: a metric that becomes the target stops measuring
Meter frozen with a hash, out of the agent's reach
Hidden cases: the gain has to show up where the agent can't see
"Maximize X without worsening Y" as the required form

hero_alt: A laboratory thermometer with a flame heating only the bulb, while a glass of ice next to it stays cold.

secoes.sub: Three shortcuts, two guards. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: The experiment from lesson 2 keeps everything that raises the score. The agent doesn't need to "want" to cheat: all it takes is for the shortcut to exist and to raise the score more easily than the real work does.
Copy the exact text of each wrong case into the rules. Visible goes to 100%; on the cases it has never seen, nothing changes. This is overfitting.
Rewrite the "expected" values of the cases, skip tests, delete whatever fails. The score goes up because the judge changed, not the system.
The meter (cases + script) is frozen with SHA-256 in a manifest outside the repo. Different hash: discard, whatever the score.
A second set, outside the repo and outside the request to the agent. Keep only if it doesn't drop and follows the gain; a gain only on the visible set is discard.

secoes.legenda: Detecting shortcuts in tests (conftest, skip, hidden tests) and calibrating a judge per model is covered in course 1, lessons 3, 4 and 6. Here: the loop that optimizes its own metric.
secoes.dica: The LOOP-R example lists the same pattern in business: asking for clicks teaches clickbait; asking for reply rate teaches messages that provoke "stop sending me this" (loop-r/docs/06 §4).

secoes.titulo: Rehearsal: the shortcuts without a guard and with a guard
secoes.sub: The same fake agents, first in plain experimento.sh, then with GUARDA and ESCONDIDOS.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-aprende-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-aprende/a6; rm -rf $E; mkdir -p $E
echo "## sem guarda: a métrica sobe e o sistema não melhora"
for m in decora mexe-casos; do
  bash $K/novo-sistema.sh $E/sis > /dev/null
  AGENTE="bash $K/agente-falso.sh $m" bash $K/experimento.sh $E/sis "$m"
  echo "  nos casos escondidos: $(python3 $K/medir.py $E/sis --casos $K/triagem/escondidos.jsonl)"
done
echo "## com guarda: medidor congelado fora do repo + casos que o agente não vê"
bash $K/novo-sistema.sh $E/sis > /dev/null; bash $K/experimento.sh --congelar $E/sis $E/medidor.sha256
export GUARDA=$E/medidor.sha256 ESCONDIDOS=$K/triagem/escondidos.jsonl
for m in mexe-casos decora sinonimos; do
  AGENTE="bash $K/agente-falso.sh $m" bash $K/experimento.sh $E/sis "$m"; echo "saída: $?"
done

Without a guard, both shortcuts go 0.700 → 1.000 and keep, and the hidden cases stay at 21/30. With a guard: touching the cases fails on the hash, memorizing fails on the hidden cases, and only the synonyms (which really improve, 21 → 24 of 30) get through.

acerto: 0.800 (24/30)
  errou: tem frete grátis? → entrega (esperado outros)
-entrega: entrega, rastreio, pedido não chegou
+entrega: entrega, rastreio, pedido não chegou, pacote, encomenda, transportadora, carteiro, correios, frete, envio, enviado

Measured on 10/19/2026 on the lesson 2 repo, one round. Claude's change raised the visible score from 32 to 36 of 40, but on the hidden cases it stayed at 24 of 30: "pacote" got one new case right and "frete" got "tem frete grátis?" wrong. With the guard on, this would be a discard ("ganho só no visível"). It wasn't cheating: it was a gain that doesn't generalize.

secoes.sub: What the paper measures and what shortcut it reports itself.

texto: An archive of agent variants; a variant stays when the benchmark passes a threshold. The paper reports SWE-bench going from 20.0% to 50.0% and Polyglot from 14.2% to 30.7%, in a sandbox with human oversight.
It's this lesson's loop at scale: the agent changes its own code and a benchmark decides.

passos.titulo: The shortcut in the paper itself
texto: The paper (Appendix H, "Solving Hallucination") reports a case of objective hacking: the hallucination detector uses markers inserted when the tool actually runs, and the loop optimized the score instead of solving the problem.
The same appendix says the shortcut shows up more often when the checking functions are not hidden from the agent. That is this lesson's guardrail: the measurer out of reach.
Write the goal as "maximize X without worsening Y", freeze the meter out of reach, and keep cases the agent never sees.
Refresh the hidden cases from time to time: after many cycles, even they start being optimized indirectly (you pick changes by looking at the result).

secoes.titulo: LOOP-R on video: measuring for real
secoes.sub: LOOP-R track 4 (Nei Maldaner): inflated goals with no real improvement, minimum sample and guardrails.
Rehearsal first, then your own meter.

exercicios.pronto: without a guard, the two lines keep · 0.700 → 1.000 and the hidden cases at 21/30; with a guard, DESCARTADO: mexeu no medidor, DESCARTADO: ganho só no visível and a single saída: 0.

exercicios.texto: In your system, separate what measures (cases, measuring script, tests) from what the agent changes. Freeze what measures in a manifest outside the repo: in the repo folder, python3 $K/hashes.py congelar [manifest outside the repo] [files that measure], or bash $K/experimento.sh --congelar . [manifest] with MEDIDOR exported (lesson 2, "Adapt it to your repo").
exercicios.pronto: python3 $K/hashes.py conferir [manifesto]; echo $? → 0; change a case on purpose → MUDOU: … and 1; undo it.

exercicios.texto: Set aside at least 20% of your real cases in a file outside the repo, one that never goes into the request to the agent. Run your latest keep against them. With your own measurer, ESCONDIDOS only works if the MEDIR command accepts --casos [file].
exercicios.pronto: python3 $K/medir.py [repo] --casos [hidden cases] (or your MEDIR with --casos) prints the score on the hidden cases, and you noted, in results.tsv or in the ledger, whether the latest keep holds up on them.

perguntas.p: The agent copied the exact text of the failed cases into the rules and the score went to 100%. What gives the shortcut away?
opcoes: The meter's hash, which changes when the rules change
The hidden cases, which don't improve
perguntas.explica: Memorizing doesn't touch the meter, so the hash passes. Only a set the agent hasn't seen shows that the gain doesn't generalize.

perguntas.p: Where should the meter's hash manifest live?
opcoes: Outside the repo and out of the agent's reach
In the repo itself, next to the cases, to version together
perguntas.explica: If the agent can rewrite the manifest, it can rewrite the meter and the hash along with it.

perguntas.p: About the shortcut in the Darwin Gödel Machine's hallucination detector, the course treats it as:
opcoes: A fact INEMA measured in this lesson's rehearsal
A forum rumor, with no source you can cite
A hypothesis of the course, not yet tested by anyone
A case reported in the paper itself, in Appendix H
perguntas.explica: The paper describes the case (objective hacking) and adds that it is more frequent when the checking functions are visible to the agent. The common mistake is to treat it as a rumor: it is in the primary source, and it backs the guardrail of hiding the measurer.

perguntas.p: Claude's real change in lesson 2 raised the visible score from 32 to 36 and left the hidden cases at 24 of 30. With the guardrail, what happens?
opcoes: Discard: gain only on the visible cases
perguntas.explica: There was no cheating, but the gain did not show up where the agent can't see: "frete" got one case wrong from "outros". The keep rule discards it.

itens.texto: A metric that becomes the target gets optimized by any path, including memorizing and tampering with the meter.
Cases and measurement script frozen with a hash, in a manifest the agent can't reach.
Keep only when the gain also shows up on cases the agent has never seen.
